answer: To mint an identity, a recruit locks a ferrous collateral bond equal to the 30-day median earnings of established miners, held for two epochs. That bond is grafted onto a vine of three prior attestors from distinct cohorts; each posts 8% of their own bond and may slash the recruit if stylometry or funding-graph overlap exceeds a published threshold. After fourteen days the recruit must pass a mesa field exam — a live, randomized protocol-design task scored by five non-overlapping juries. Failed or copied exams forfeit the bond to those juries, so farms pay per identity and per failure.
